title: Checkpoint: Full Layout Report
prompt:
Given
 
```c
struct Record { char kind; long id; char active; double score; };
```
 
implement `void program(void)` printing exactly one layout line:
 
```
kind@0 id@8 active@16 score@24 size:32 pad:0
```
 
All numbers must come from `offsetof`/`sizeof` measured on a locally defined identical struct (`<stddef.h>`); `pad:` is the *trailing* padding — size minus (last member offset + last member size). Internal padding before `score` is not counted. On a second line, print the contract class of signed overflow by calling `classify_overflow()`, which you also implement and which returns exactly `"undefined"`.

tests.name: layout line
tests.code:
const char* out = cj_capture(program);
CHECK_CONTAINS(out, "kind@0 id@8 active@16 score@24 size:32");
tests.hint: long is 8-aligned here, so id lands at 8; double at 24; total 32 is already a multiple of 8.

tests.name: trailing pad is zero
tests.hint: size 32 minus (offset 24 + 8) = 0 — the 7 missing bytes are INTERNAL padding before score, not trailing.

tests.name: overflow class
tests.hint: Signed overflow is undefined behavior — print what your own classify_overflow returns.
